subject.title: Reject unsupported diagnostics OTel grpc config

question: Should upgrading a released `diagnostics.otel.protocol: "grpc"` configuration through Doctor remove the unsupported value and disable enabled OTLP telemetry when active signals would fail, rather than preserve `enabled: true` and require a collector change first?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically focused and tested, but choosing the user-visible migration outcome for a formerly accepted persisted configuration is a compatibility and operator-policy decision that code review cannot safely infer.

options.title: Approve the conservative migration
options.body: Keep the proposed Doctor behavior: remove `grpc`, disable only incompatible enabled OTLP telemetry, and preserve stdout-only logging.

options.title: Preserve enabled state
options.body: Remove `grpc` but leave telemetry enabled so operators immediately choose an OTLP/HTTP endpoint after upgrade.

options.title: Keep grpc accepted temporarily
options.body: Defer schema narrowing until maintainers choose a broader deprecation window or an actual gRPC exporter path.

recommendation.title: Approve the conservative migration
recommendation.body: Keep the proposed Doctor behavior: remove `grpc`, disable only incompatible enabled OTLP telemetry, and preserve stdout-only logging.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline routes the compatibility decision to this explicitly notified maintainer-facing contact.
